$comment: Vendored copy of the peck-view/v1 contract (source sha256 af97b2574a086282b4adeaca2ccaf5348acbbf5b5b5275338bc677b7e5ddba03). Written by scripts/sync-peck-view.mjs; do not edit by hand.
title: PeckView
description: peck-view/v1: the hydrated read model served by the overlay under /v2. The overlay (producer) owns this contract; clients and the SDK consume it. Every view is viewer-independent: nothing in a PostView, ThreadView, ProfileView or FeedPage depends on who asks, so responses can be cached by URL. Per-viewer facts (liked by me, following, blocked) live only in ViewerState. Evolution rules: within v1 the overlay may ADD optional properties and ADD enum values documented as open; it never removes, renames or retypes a property. Consumers must ignore properties they do not know. A breaking change is a new contract version (peck-view/v2) served side by side. The producer validates its own responses strictly (additionalProperties: false), so a leaked database column fails the overlay's own contract tests. TypeScript types are generated from this schema.

Txid.title: Txid
Txid.description: A BSV transaction id: 64 lowercase hex characters.

Key.title: Key
Key.description: A signing key as the chain carries it: either a base58 P2PKH address (1…) or a 66-hex compressed secp256k1 public key (02…/03…).

IdentityKey.title: IdentityKey
IdentityKey.description: A BRC-100 identity key: a 66-hex compressed secp256k1 public key, lowercase.

AuthorView.title: AuthorView
AuthorView.description: Who signed a post, resolved once on the overlay. Every AuthorView comes from the same resolution, so all clients show the same name, handle and picture for the same key. Identity is keyed on keys, never on names: `key` is the on-chain signer and `identityKey` the BRC-100 identity it resolves to. Names, handles and pictures are labels that can change between reads.

key.description: The key that signed the post, exactly as indexed: a base58 P2PKH address, or a 66-hex compressed public key for agent and BRC-100-native authors. Constant for the post. Use it as the profile fallback when `handle` and `identityKey` are null.

address.description: P2PKH address of `key`: equal to `key` when `key` is an address, derived from the public key otherwise. Null only when `key` is neither.

identityKey.description: BRC-100 identity key that `key` belongs to. First match wins: (1) overlay identity resolution (key-binding, light identity attestations, ProfileToken, handle claims); (2) the identity key recorded on a legacy peck.to account for this address; (3) `key` itself when it is a public key. Null when nothing links the key to an identity. Prefer it over `key` as the person's id when present. Always null for custodial relay keys.

handle.description: Canonical handle without the leading @, from on-chain claims only: light handle claims > HandleToken > the ProfileToken's own handle field. Resolved on every read, so it can move to a new owner; the key cannot. Null when unclaimed, and always null for custodial relay keys.

displayName.description: The name to render. Never empty. Candidates in order, first non-empty wins, and `nameSource` records which one: identity > tx > account > external > paymail > key (see nameSource). For custodial relay keys only tx, external and key are considered, because the key belongs to the app.

nameSource.description: Where `displayName` came from. identity: the author's own on-chain profile (light identity attestation preferred over ProfileToken). tx: the display_name written into this transaction's MAP data (for custodial relays that is the app's claim about its user). account: the legacy peck.to account row (off-chain). external: an off-chain platform profile such as twetch; never written on-chain, render with a provenance marker. paymail: the local part of the account paymail. key: nothing named the author; `displayName` is the shortened key (first 6 + … + last 4).

avatarUrl.description: URL of the author's own picture, ready for an . Null when the author has no usable picture; peck-native clients then show `generatedAvatarUrl`, others a monogram. Mapping from `avatarRef`, the only place it is done: uhrp:// → /uhrp/; b:// → /b/ (/xavatar/, a downscaling proxy, when the picture comes from an external profile); ord:// → /ord/; https:// and http:// URLs pass through; data:image/* URIs pass through; peck.to's own generated /avatar/ URLs count as no picture; anything else maps to null. The media base and the UHRP host are set by the overlay operator; the media base is https://peck.to by default.

avatarRef.description: The picture reference exactly as published, before mapping (uhrp://, b://, ord://, https://, data:image/…). Null when the winning record has no picture reference.

avatarSource.description: Which record the picture came from: identity (on-chain profile), account (legacy peck.to account row) or external (off-chain platform profile, b:// uploads only; other twetch picture formats are dead links). The first record whose reference maps to a URL wins, in that order. Null when `avatarUrl` is null.

generatedAvatarUrl.description: Deterministic generated avatar (the peck bird) for this key: <media base>/avatar/<key>?seed=<address>. The seed is the P2PKH address so one key gets the same bird on every surface. Always present.

paymail.description: Paymail on the legacy peck.to account row for this key, if any. Off-chain.

custodialRelay.description: Set when `key` is a known shared custodial key (e.g. treechat.io): the app signed on its users' behalf, so `key` identifies the app, not the person. The value names the app. Null otherwise.

external.description: Set when the name or the picture came from an off-chain platform profile (nameSource or avatarSource is external). Null otherwise.

sourceHandle.description: An alias the key holds in another protocol's own namespace (a Zanaadu user number, @14), shown next to the key and never as a peck handle. Absent when the key holds none. Carried on the authors of Zanaadu posts and on profiles; other surfaces may leave it out. Optional within v1.

SourceHandle.title: SourceHandle
SourceHandle.description: A name a key holds in another protocol's registry. It lives in that protocol's namespace: render it with the namespace (@14 · zanaadu), never as a handle of this network.

namespace.description: Whose namespace the alias lives in: zanaadu. Open set.

value.description: The alias as the source shows it, e.g. @14.

number.description: The user number itself. When the key owns several, the lowest (which one the source shows is not proven).

kind.description: What sort of alias this is: a numbered registry entry the source lets users buy and move, not a chosen name. Open set.

numbers.description: Every number the key owns, ascending. Present only when it owns more than one.

membershipProof.description: Whether the overlay verified the entry against the registry's merkle root. none: the number is derived from the registry's own counter, membership is not proven.

ExternalProfileRef.title: ExternalProfileRef
ExternalProfileRef.description: Where an off-chain name or picture came from. The binding between the account and the key lives only in that platform's database, not on-chain.

source.description: The platform the profile was read from, e.g. twetch.

externalId.description: The account id on that platform, when known.

PostCounts.title: PostCounts
PostCounts.description: Aggregates about a post. All are counted live at read time except lockedSats and powBits, which the indexer materializes on the post row.

likes.description: Reaction records targeting this post, all of them (the same number /v1/post reports): not unique reactors.

replies.description: Direct replies: posts whose parent is this post.

reposts.description: Posts of type repost that reference this post.

quotes.description: Posts of any other type that reference this post with their own content.

tipSats.description: Satoshis the chain shows reached this post's author from payments that name this post (MAP type=payment, tx=<this post>), summed over every indexed payment: P2PKH outputs to the author's signing address, a BRC-29 output whose payment record publishes its key linkage, or Twetch's author share of a paid action. A payment's own claimed `value` is never counted, so a BRC-29 tip that does not publish its linkage adds nothing.

lockedSats.description: Satoshis locked against this post (MAP type=lock commitments), as materialized on the post row.

powBits.description: Summed difficulty bits of valid proof-of-work boosts, as materialized on the post row.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: What the chain says about who stands behind a post, graded once on the overlay.

grade.description: Decided in this order. custodial: signed by a known shared custodial key, or app is treechat; the signer is the app, not the person (decided first because it rests on facts the index always holds). key: the Author Identity Protocol signature was verified against the author key. unverified: no verified signature on record; a statement about the index, not proof of forgery (some apps sign over preimage variants the verifier does not check). Posts carried by another protocol (PostView.source) are graded unverified: they carry no AIP signature, and source.commitment says what they carry instead.

aipVerified.description: The indexer's raw AIP verification flag. Null when the indexer never checked.

nameInTx.description: The display_name written into the transaction itself (MAP), if any. For custodial relays this is the only name the chain carries.

MediaItem.title: MediaItem
MediaItem.description: One piece of binary media carried by a post's transaction.

url.description: Fetchable URL: <media base>/b/<txid> for the B-protocol body, <media base>/b/<txid>?vout=<vout> for an extra output. The media base defaults to https://peck.to, whose /b/ proxy serves only sniffed raster/audio/video types from the chain.

mediaType.description: Declared media type (image/jpeg, video/mp4, …) as written on-chain. Clients must not trust it for security decisions.

vout.description: Output index for an extra output. Null for the post's main B body.

sizeBytes.description: Size in bytes when the index knows it; null otherwise.

Geo.title: Geo
Geo.description: Where a post was placed, as the author wrote it on chain (MAP lat, lng and optionally category). The coordinates are WGS84 degrees.

category.description: What kind of place this is, from MAP category, lowercase: peck.world writes general, business, event, alert, idea or photo. Open set; treat null and unknown values as general. Optional within v1: absent only from overlays that predate it.

ParentStub.title: ParentStub
ParentStub.description: Just enough of a reply's parent to render 'Replying to <name>'. The full parent is in ThreadView.parent.

author.description: The parent's author. Null when the parent is not indexed.

PostView.title: PostView
PostView.description: One post, hydrated for rendering: author, counts, media, provenance, one level of referenced post and a stub of the parent. Viewer-independent. Every PostView comes from the same hydration step, whether it is served in a feed, a thread or a batch.

txid.description: The post's transaction id (64 lowercase hex); its permanent address.

type.description: Bitcoin Schema MAP type as indexed: post, reply or repost today. Open set: other values (e.g. function_response) may appear; render unknown types as a post. Posts carried by another protocol (see `source`) use post, reply and vote; a vote has no text of its own, and source.vote names its target. A location never changes the type: a pin is a post (or reply, or repost) whose `geo` is set, and a pin written with the legacy MAP type pin is served as type post with kind pin. object is a located object that is not a post (a place registered by an app such as locus): it always has `geo`, usually has no text, and a text feed can leave it out by asking for types=post,reply,repost.

kind.description: Content kind from MAP (e.g. longform, note), lowercase. Null when unset. pin marks a post written with the legacy MAP type pin (peck.world before June 2026); it renders exactly like any other post with a location. Never filter pins by kind: most pins have no kind, and `geo` is what makes a post a pin.

app.description: The MAP app that wrote the transaction (peck.to, twetch, treechat, …), or zanaadu for Zanaadu posts, replies and votes (see `source`). Null when unset.

createdAt.description: When the post was made (the indexed timestamp), ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z.

blockHeight.description: Block the transaction was mined in. Null while unconfirmed (the index stores 0 or NULL for those).

text.description: The text body: MAP content, falling back to the B content. Null when the body is binary media (see `media`) or empty. Untrusted user input: sanitize before rendering it as markup.

mediaType.description: B-protocol media type of the body as written on-chain (text/plain, text/markdown, image/jpeg, …). Null when unset. Use it to pick a renderer, e.g. markdown for text/markdown.

textTruncated.description: True when `text` was cut to the response limit. Limits, in characters (Unicode code points): 262144 for ThreadView.post, 16384 for every other post (feeds, batches, replies, parents, embedded refs). GET /v2/post/{txid} returns the long form.

textLength.description: Length of the full text in characters (Unicode code points), before truncation. 0 when `text` is null.

media.description: Media carried by the transaction: the B body when its media type is image/*, audio/* or video/*, followed by every extra output the index holds for the transaction, in vout order, whatever its type. Empty when there is none.

tags.description: MAP tags, trimmed, empty ones dropped. The index stores them as one comma-joined string, so a tag that itself contains a comma arrives split.

channel.description: The channel this post names in its own MAP `channel` field, as written. A reply or a repost is not placed in its parent's channel: it reports a channel only when it names one itself, and peck.to's clients never write one on a reply, so a client that wants to show where a thread lives reads the thread root's `channel`. /v1 serves the same value. Null when unset.

geo.description: Location attached to the post: set when the transaction carries a MAP lat and lng in range. (0, 0) counts as no location. Every app reads the same field, so a location written by one app (peck.to, peck.world, …) shows in all of them. Null when the post has none.

parentTxid.description: The post this one replies to. Null for top-level posts.

threadRootTxid.description: The thread root as materialized by the indexer, or null. Not filled for most replies yet: walk parentTxid when you need the root.

parent.description: Stub of the parent for 'Replying to'. Null exactly when parentTxid is null, and always null on an embedded `ref`.

refTxid.description: The post this one reposts or quotes: the indexed reference; for older posts without one, a MAP quote target ({"subcontext":"quote","tx":…}) or the first twetch.com/t/<txid> link in the text.

refKind.description: repost: type is repost, the post re-shares `ref` without content of its own. quote: the post has its own content and embeds `ref`. Null exactly when refTxid is null.

ref.description: The referenced post, embedded one level deep: its own `ref` and `parent` are always null (its refTxid/parentTxid are kept). Null when refTxid is null or the target is not indexed; render a link to refTxid then.

paywalled.description: True when the overlay withheld text and media because the operator's paywall covers the post (text null, media empty). /v2 never unlocks content per viewer. The paywall is disabled in production, so this is false today.

source.description: Present when the post is carried by another protocol than Bitcoin Schema (today: Zanaadu). Such a post has no AIP signature, so provenance.grade is unverified and aipVerified null; its integrity is source.commitment, which is what a renderer shows instead of the AIP grade. Absent for Bitcoin Schema posts. Optional within v1.

PostSource.title: PostSource
PostSource.description: What the chain proves about a post carried by another protocol, and only that. For Zanaadu: the text sits in a transaction input under a covenant, committed to by a sha256 hash; the transaction pays a fixed platform fee; its other outputs go to one-time addresses and cannot be attributed to anyone, so they are never counted as tips or earnings.

protocol.description: The protocol that carries the post: zanaadu. Open set.

action.description: The source's own verb for the transaction, untranslated: xanapost, xanareply, xanaupvote or xanadownvote for Zanaadu. Open set.

commitment.description: The integrity commitment the transaction carries. Null when none was recorded.

feeSats.description: The platform fee the transaction paid: the one payment that is proven on-chain (a fixed amount to a fixed address). It is what the poster paid, not what anyone earned.

unattributedOutputs.description: How many other outputs the transaction has that cannot be attributed to anyone (change and payments look alike). Null when not recorded.

unattributedSats.description: Their total in satoshis. Never a tip or an earning. Null when not recorded.

vote.description: For a vote (type vote): its direction and target. Null for posts and replies.

ContentCommitment.title: ContentCommitment
ContentCommitment.description: A hash the transaction commits to, and whether the overlay verified it.

covers.description: What is hashed: text, the post's full text (posts, replies); target, the target's txid (votes). Open set.

verified.description: True when the overlay found the commitment in the transaction and, for text, the hash of the text it serves equals it.

location.description: Where in the transaction the commitment was found, as the source format names it. Null when not recorded.

SourceVote.title: SourceVote
SourceVote.description: A vote on another post, as the source records it.

direction.description: Up or down, from the topic the vote was admitted to.

targetTxid.description: The post voted on (open it with GET /v2/post/{txid}). Null when the source no longer holds it.

amountSats.description: The amount the vote carries in its data. Its recipient cannot be proven, so it is not a payment to anyone. Null when absent.

ThreadView.title: ThreadView
ThreadView.description: Response of GET /v2/post/{txid}: the requested post (`post`, text up to 262144 characters), its direct parent and every descendant reply, hydrated in one response.

parent.description: The post it replies to, fully hydrated. Null for a top-level post or when the parent is not indexed.

replies.description: All descendants of `post`, level by level (children before grandchildren), oldest first within a level. Build the tree from each reply's parentTxid.

repliesTruncated.description: True when the descendant walk stopped at its cap (500 replies or 10 levels), so `replies` is incomplete.

FeedCursor.title: FeedCursor
FeedCursor.description: Keyset position after the last item of a page, in the structured-cursor form before_<sort column>=<value>. Send every key and value back unchanged as query parameters, together with the same filters, to get the next page. The keys follow the sort columns of the chosen rank (before_ts and before_txid for rank=latest), so treat them as opaque.

FeedPage.title: FeedPage
FeedPage.description: One page of a feed (GET /v2/feed, and later search and profile feeds). There is no total count by design.

items.description: The posts on this page, in feed order.

next.description: Cursor for the next page. Null when this is the last page.

PostBatch.title: PostBatch
PostBatch.description: Response of POST /v2/posts: many posts by txid in one call.

posts.description: The posts that were found, in request order.

missing.description: Requested txids that are not indexed.

ProfileCounts.title: ProfileCounts
ProfileCounts.description: Social graph counts for a profile.

followers.description: Follow records pointing at any of the profile's keys or its handle.

following.description: Follow records made by any of the profile's keys.

posts.description: Indexed posts of every type (posts, replies, reposts) signed by any of the profile's keys: what GET /v2/feed?author=<keys> pages through. Counted live. Optional within v1: absent only from overlays that predate it.

IdentityCertificate.title: IdentityCertificate
IdentityCertificate.description: One attribute certified for an identity (an account on a platform, an email address), with every certifier that attests it. Only certificates that were published for the identity, are issued to it, carry a valid certifier signature and are not revoked on-chain are listed. Clients decide which certifiers they trust.

platform.description: Lowercase id of the certificate type's platform: x, discord, email, google, github, peck. Open set: unknown for a certificate type the overlay does not recognise; render unknown values generically.

value.description: The certified identifier to show: the first non-empty of the certificate's userName, username, handle, name, email or sub fields, else its first non-empty field. Null when the certificate carries none. Untrusted user text.

certifiers.description: Public keys of the certifiers whose certificates attest this platform and value, sorted, no duplicates.

certificateHashes.description: SHA-256 content hashes (UHRP addresses) of those certificate documents, sorted, so a client can fetch and verify them itself.

ProfileView.title: ProfileView
ProfileView.description: Response of GET /v2/profile/{key|@handle|name}: an identity's header. The path segment is an address, a public key, an on-chain handle (with or without @), or a legacy peck.to account name (its username, paymail, or the paymail's local part); an on-chain handle wins over an account name. `author` is baked exactly like a post author; author.key is the key the profile was looked up by (the handle owner's identity key for handle lookups, the account's address for account names). Its posts come from GET /v2/feed?author=… (a FeedPage).

bio.description: Bio from the identity profile attestation, else the ProfileToken, else the legacy account row. Untrusted user text. Null when none.

profileOutpoint.description: Outpoint (<txid>.<vout>) of the canonical profile record the name and picture came from, when on-chain.

keys.description: Every key known to sign for this identity: the identity key, its P2PKH address, and bound signing keys with their addresses. Posts authored by any of them belong to the profile.

certificates.description: Verified certificates of the identity, one entry per platform and value, ordered by platform then value. Empty when the profile has no identity key or none verify. Optional within v1: absent from overlays that predate it, and from an answer that could not verify them in time (such an answer is not cacheable).

PostViewerState.title: PostViewerState
PostViewerState.description: What one viewer has done to one post.

liked.description: The viewer (any of ViewerState.keys) has a reaction on this post.

reposted.description: The viewer has a post of type repost referencing this post.

AuthorViewerState.title: AuthorViewerState
AuthorViewerState.description: The viewer's relationship to one author.

following.description: The viewer has a follow record for this author (by any of its keys or its handle).

blocked.description: The viewer has a block record for this author.

muted.description: The viewer has a mute record for this author.

ViewerState.title: ViewerState
ViewerState.description: Response of POST /v2/viewer/state: the only per-viewer read in /v2. Built from public on-chain records looked up by the viewer's key; never cached by the overlay.

viewer.description: The viewer key the state was computed for, as given.

keys.description: Every key treated as the viewer: the given key, its identity key, bound signing keys and their addresses.

authors.description: State per requested author key, keyed exactly as requested.

AppCount.title: AppCount
AppCount.description: How many posts one MAP app has written.

app.description: The MAP app name as indexed (peck.to, twetch, treechat, ...), exactly the value GET /v2/feed?app= filters on.

count.description: Posts of the requested types written by this app. As of AppList.asOf, not live.

AppList.title: AppList
AppList.description: The apps that have written posts, most posts first (GET /v2/apps): what an app filter chip row needs. Counts are materialized, not live: they are as old as `asOf`, refreshed in the background about every 5 minutes. Counts cover exactly the posts GET /v2/feed serves and can filter on.

apps.description: Ordered by count descending, then by app name. Apps with no posts of the requested types are absent.

asOf.description: When these counts were taken, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z.

Reaction.title: Reaction
Reaction.description: One like or repost of a post, and who made it.

kind.description: like: a like record of the post. repost: a post of type repost that references it. Open set: render an unknown kind generically.

txid.description: The transaction that made the reaction: the like, or the repost post (open it with GET /v2/post/{txid}). Null for likes indexed without their transaction id.

createdAt.description: When the reaction was made (the indexed timestamp), ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z.

emoji.description: The like's emoji as written on-chain (twetch upvotes arrive as ⬆︎). Null for reposts and for likes without one. Untrusted user text.

actorKey.description: Who reacted, exactly as indexed. Usually a key (a P2PKH address or a public key); some imported likes carry only a placeholder such as unknown or scripthash:…, and then `author` is null.

author.description: Who reacted, baked exactly like a post author, so the name, handle and picture match that person's posts. For a repost it carries the name the repost transaction gives (custodial relays name their users there). Null when actorKey is not a key.

ReactionPage.title: ReactionPage
ReactionPage.description: Response of GET /v2/post/{txid}/reactions?kind=like|repost: who liked or reposted a post, newest first, a page at a time (limit 1-100, default 50). Every like record and every repost is listed, including reactors without a usable key, so the pages add up to PostCounts.likes and PostCounts.reposts. Quotes are posts with their own text and are not listed here. An unknown or not yet indexed txid is an empty page, not an error.

items.description: The reactions on this page, newest first.

next.description: Cursor for the next page, in the same structured form as FeedPage.next (before_ts with before_actor for likes, with before_txid for reposts); send it back with the same txid and kind. Null when this is the last page.

SiteStats.title: SiteStats
SiteStats.description: Response of GET /v2/stats: the site totals a sidebar shows. Both numbers are the database planner's row estimates, not counts: close to the truth on a large table, updated as the database re-analyzes it, and never exact to the post. Render them rounded (2.6M posts).

posts.description: Indexed posts of every type (posts, replies, reposts), estimated. 0 on a database never analyzed.

accounts.description: Legacy peck.to accounts, estimated. On-chain identities without an account are not counted.

estimated.description: Always true: the numbers are estimates. Present so a client can never mistake them for counts.

asOf.description: When the estimates were read, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z.

ChannelName.title: ChannelName
ChannelName.description: The name of a channel. Channels are an open namespace: nobody owns a name, and a channel exists as soon as a post or message names it. Case-sensitive and matched exactly (GET /v2/feed?channel= takes the same value). Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters, so a name is safe in a URL path segment. Names that do not fit are never listed.

PostingChannel.title: PostingChannel
PostingChannel.description: A channel that posts were written in recently, and how many.

posts.description: Posts, replies and reposts written in this channel since ChannelList.postingSince: the posts GET /v2/feed?channel= serves with types=post,reply,repost. Authors and apps the overlay operator hides from every feed are not counted. As of ChannelList.asOf.

ChatRoom.title: ChatRoom
ChatRoom.description: A chat room: a channel that messages were sent to.

messages.description: Messages sent to the room, all time. Private (direct) messages are never counted or listed. As of ChannelList.asOf.

lastAt.description: When the latest message was sent, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z. Null only when every message of the room was indexed without a time.

ChannelList.title: ChannelList
ChannelList.description: The channels people write in (GET /v2/channels), for a channel picker or a sidebar. Two lists, because the two kinds of activity differ: `posting` ranks channels by the posts written in them recently, `rooms` ranks chat rooms by their latest message. A name can be in both. Nothing here depends on the viewer, and counts are as old as `asOf`. The legacy room `global` is the global chat itself, not a room, and is never listed.

posting.description: Most posts first, ties by name. Empty when nothing was posted to a channel in the window.

rooms.description: Latest message first, ties by name.

postingSince.description: The start of the window `posting` counts over, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z. Currently the 30 days before `asOf`: read this field rather than assuming the length.

asOf.description: When these lists were read, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z.

MessageView.title: MessageView
MessageView.description: One chat message: written to a channel or to the global chat, or sent privately to one recipient. Built from the message transaction (MAP type=message). Nothing here depends on the viewer. A direct (private) message carries whatever its sender wrote: clients that encrypt their direct messages (peck.to does) put the ciphertext in `text`, and the overlay never decrypts or inspects it.

createdAt.description: When the message was indexed, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z. Messages are ordered by this time, ties by txid.

author.description: Who sent the message, baked exactly like a post author, so the name, handle and picture match that person's posts. Always present: a sender the chain does not name carries the shortened key as displayName.

text.description: The message body: MAP content, falling back to the B content. Null when the body is binary media (see `mediaType`) or withheld by the paywall. Untrusted user input: sanitize before rendering it as markup.

textLength.description: Length of the full text in characters (Unicode code points), before truncation. 0 when `text` is null.

textTruncated.description: True when `text` was cut to the response limit of 65536 characters (Unicode code points).

mediaType.description: B-protocol media type of the body as written on-chain (text/plain, text/markdown, image/jpeg, …). Null when unset.

app.description: The MAP app that wrote the transaction (peck.to, bitchat, …). Null when unset. Agents and bots usually write from their own app name.

channel.description: The channel the message was written to, as written (case-sensitive; a channel name is not always a ChannelName). Null for the global chat (a message without a channel, or in the legacy room `global`) and for direct messages.

recipient.description: For a direct message, the identity key it is addressed to, exactly as written on-chain (the MAP bapID). Null for a message to a channel or to the global chat.

direct.description: True for a private message: one addressed to a recipient. Direct messages are only listed when the request names a recipient or an author without a room, never in a channel or in the global chat.

paywalled.description: True when the overlay withheld the text because the operator's paywall covers channel messages (text null). /v2 never unlocks content per viewer, and direct messages are never paywalled. The paywall is disabled in production, so this is false today.

MessagePage.title: MessagePage
MessagePage.description: One page of chat messages (GET /v2/messages), a page at a time (limit 1-100, default 50). The default order is newest first, so the first page is the latest conversation: render it oldest-first by reversing `items`, and send `next` to load the page before it ("load older"). With order=asc the page runs oldest first from a given point, which is how a client asks "what is new since my last message". There is no total count by design. Only public chain data is listed; direct messages are the on-chain records (their text is as written by the sender, normally ciphertext).

items.description: The messages on this page, in the order asked for: newest first by default, oldest first with order=asc.

next.description: Cursor for the next page in the direction of travel, in the same structured form as FeedPage.next: before_ts with before_txid (older messages, order=desc), after_ts with after_txid (newer messages, order=asc). Send it back unchanged with the same filters. Null exactly when there are no more messages in that direction.

IdentityList.title: IdentityList
IdentityList.description: The identities on the overlay, newest first (GET /v2/identities): who is on peck. An identity is a BRC-100 identity key that has published a profile. A key that is bound to another identity as one of its signing keys is folded into that identity and not listed on its own. Every item is baked exactly like a post author, so the name, handle and picture match that person's posts. An identity that published no name and holds no handle carries the shortened key as displayName (nameSource key): render it as a wallet identity.

items.description: At most `limit` identities. Identities with an on-chain light profile come first, the latest attested first; then those known only from a ProfileToken, the latest minted first.

total.description: How many identities the overlay lists in all, not the size of this page.

AuthorListItem.title: AuthorListItem
AuthorListItem.description: One author in the ranked author list: who they are and how much they have posted.

author.description: Who the row is, baked exactly like a post author, so the name, handle and picture match that person's posts. For a shared custodial key (see custodialRelay) the row is the app, not a person. With by=name the row is one name an app's users post under: `displayName` is that name (nameSource tx) and `key` the shared key they post through.

posts.description: How many posts, replies and reposts the row has written (likes, follows and other non-content records are not counted), as of AuthorList.asOf. Limited to one app when the request named `app`.

lastPostAt.description: When the latest of those posts was indexed, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z. Null only when none of them carries a time.

app.description: The MAP app the row posts from: the requested `app`, or, without one, the app that has most of the key's posts (ties by name). Null when the posts name no app.

AuthorList.title: AuthorList
AuthorList.description: Authors whose public, on-chain posts the overlay indexes, ranked by how much they posted (GET /v2/authors): the people "across Bitcoin", from twetch, treechat and the other apps that write the same schema, whether or not they ever claimed a peck identity (see IdentityList for those). A snapshot of the ranking is refreshed about every ten minutes; `asOf` says when. Only the top 5000 of a ranking are listed (a discovery surface, not a census). Rows the overlay operator hides from every feed are left out, so a listed row does not open on an empty feed. Keyset paged. An overlay that has not finished computing its first snapshot answers 503 with the `timeout` error code: retry in a few seconds.

items.description: The authors on this page, most posts first, ties by key in byte order (by name when by=name).

next.description: Cursor for the next page, in the same structured form as FeedPage.next: before_posts with before_key (the last row's post count and its key, or its name with by=name). Send it back unchanged with the same filters. Null exactly when this is the last page.

total.description: How many rows the ranking holds for these filters, as of `asOf`: at most 5000 (see `capped`), not a census of everyone.

capped.description: True when the ranking had more rows than it lists and was cut to the 5000 with most posts.

asOf.description: When the ranking was computed, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z. Counts and order are as old as this.

LensRule.title: LensRule
LensRule.description: One rule of a moderation lens.

match.description: What the rule looks at. author: `value` is a P2PKH address. txid: a post. app: an app name. category: a classification label such as spam. tag and geo are recorded but not applied by GET /v2/feed yet. Open set: ignore a rule whose match you do not know.

value.description: What to match, in the form `match` names.

action.description: hide is the only action GET /v2/feed applies today; downrank and label are recorded for later. Open set: ignore a rule whose action you do not know.

label.description: The text a `label` rule shows. Optional, and only on rules that carry one.

Lens.title: Lens
Lens.description: A published, subscribable moderation lens: a rule set its issuer signed and a reader can apply to their own feeds. Filtering, never deletion: the posts stay on chain and in the index, and a reader who does not subscribe still sees them. Subscribe by passing `lensId` as `lens` to GET /v2/feed. Only the current version of a lens is listed.

lensId.description: The lens's stable id, the value GET /v2/feed?lens= takes. It stays the same across new versions of the lens.

issuer.description: Who published the lens, baked like a post author. `issuer.key` is the identity key that signed it.

scope.description: What the issuer says the lens is for (curated, for example). Free text chosen by the issuer.

rules.description: The lens's rules, in the order the issuer published them. Rules whose shape this overlay does not understand are left out, so the list can be empty.

jurisdiction.description: The legal jurisdiction the issuer attached to the lens, if any.

serial.description: The issuer's serial for this version, as published. Opaque: compare it for equality, do not order by it. Null when the lens carries none.

outpoint.description: The on-chain output that holds this version of the lens: <txid>.<vout>.

LensList.title: LensList
LensList.description: The published moderation lenses (GET /v2/lenses), newest first, for a lens picker. Nothing here depends on the viewer. A lens changes only when its issuer publishes a new version.

NotificationPost.title: NotificationPost
NotificationPost.description: Just enough of a post to say which one a notification is about: its id, type and the start of its text. Open the post with GET /v2/post/{txid} for the rest.

type.description: Bitcoin Schema MAP type as indexed (post, reply, repost, ...), as PostView.type.

text.description: The start of the text body (MAP content, falling back to the B content), at most 280 characters (Unicode code points). Null when the body is binary media or empty. Untrusted user input: render it as text, or sanitize it before rendering it as markup.

textLength.description: Length of the full text in characters (Unicode code points). 0 when `text` is null.

textTruncated.description: True when `text` is only the start of the body.

mediaType.description: B-protocol media type of the body as written on-chain (text/plain, text/markdown, image/jpeg, ...). Null when unset.

NotificationView.title: NotificationView
NotificationView.description: One thing somebody else did that concerns the viewer, built from a public on-chain record: a reply to one of the viewer's posts, a post that mentions them, a like, repost or tip of one of their posts, a follow, or a friend record naming them. What the viewer did themselves is never listed.

id.description: Stable id of this notification within the viewer's list: the same record is the same id on every read. A client may remember the ids it has shown (a read marker); the overlay keeps no read state. Treat it as opaque.

kind.description: reply: a reply to one of the viewer's posts. mention: a post that names the viewer (a MAP mention of one of their keys); a reply to the viewer that also mentions them is listed once, as the reply. like, repost, tip: of one of the viewer's posts. follow: a follow record of one of the viewer's keys or handle forms, once per follower (its latest). friend_request: a friend record naming the viewer's identity. friend_accepted: the same, when the viewer had already sent the actor one (their answer to the viewer's request). Open set: render an unknown kind generically.

createdAt.description: When the record was indexed, ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z. Notifications are ordered by this time, newest first, ties by id. Null when the record carries no usable time (some imported follows); those sort last.

actorKey.description: Who did it, exactly as indexed: usually a key (a P2PKH address or a public key; an identity key for friend records). Some imported records carry only a placeholder such as unknown, and then `actor` is null.

actor.description: Who did it, baked exactly like a post author, so the name, handle and picture match that person's posts. Null when actorKey is not a key.

txid.description: The transaction that made it: the reply or the mentioning post, the like, the repost, the payment. Null for follows and friend records (indexed without one) and for likes indexed without their transaction id.

post.description: What the actor wrote: the reply (reply) or the post (mention). Null for the other kinds, and when the post is not indexed.

subject.description: The viewer's post this is about: the post replied to (reply), liked (like), reposted (repost) or tipped (tip). Null for mention, follow and the friend kinds.

sats.description: tip only: the satoshis the chain shows reached the post's author (the payment's indexed amount, never the sender's claim; the same amount PostCounts.tipSats sums). Null for the other kinds.

emoji.description: like only: the like's emoji as written on-chain, as Reaction.emoji. Null for the other kinds and for likes without one. Untrusted user text.

NotificationPage.title: NotificationPage
NotificationPage.description: Response of GET /v2/notifications?viewer=<key>: what other people did that concerns one person, newest first, a page at a time (limit 1-100, default 50). Built from public on-chain records looked up by the viewer's keys (the same set ViewerState.keys lists), so no session is needed; it depends on the viewer, so it is never cached (Cache-Control: no-store). There is no total and no unread count: the overlay keeps no read state. Replies, likes, reposts and tips are looked up on the viewer's newest 2000 posts (see `capped`).

viewer.description: The viewer key the page was computed for, as given.

keys.description: Every key treated as the viewer: the given key, its address, its identity key, the identity's bound signing keys and their addresses, and a legacy account's address. Shared custodial keys are never among them.

items.description: The notifications on this page, newest first.

next.description: Cursor for the next (older) page, in the same structured form as FeedPage.next: before_ts with before_id. Send it back unchanged with the same viewer and kinds. Null exactly when there is nothing older.

capped.description: True when the viewer has more than 2000 posts: replies, likes, reposts and tips on their older posts are not listed. Mentions, follows and friend records are always complete.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code: bad_request, not_found, timeout (a search lane gave up; retry later) or internal.

message.description: Human-readable detail. Not stable; do not parse.
